transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. It's probably just a small thing, really. 

I'm a retail supervisor, and... well, I came in because lately, when I try to explain the inventory numbers to my team, or, you know, go over the weekend schedule, my words just sort of... they start jumping around a bit. Like, I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then suddenly I'm on about Thursdays, or the church grill, and then my boss’s tone of voice. 

It's nothing too serious, I don't think, but... people just look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying. I always try to be a good supervisor and communicate clearly, so I thought I should probably ask a professional. Does that make sense, Doctor? Is that something you might be able to help me with?
Are you experiencing these difficulties with your words jumping around in conversations outside of work as well?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? But it's really not that bad outside of work, I don't think. Mostly just when I'm tired, you know? 

Like, if I'm at the grocery store or talking to my neighbor... sometimes I might lose my train of thought for a second, but I think everyone does that, right? It's just normal aging, probably. I always try to be polite and make sense when I'm chatting with folks. I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is. Does that sound like a normal thing to happen when you're just a bit worn out, Doctor?
Do you ever hear or see things that other people don't?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I mean, I know that's something doctors have to ask about, but I promise I'm not... you know, I'm not seeing things or hearing voices or anything scary like that. 

Sometimes, if it's really quiet, I might think I hear the phone ringing at the store, or someone calling my name from the next aisle over, but... that's just because I'm so used to being at work, right? It's just my brain playing tricks on me because I want to be ready to help. It's totally normal to think you hear your name when you're a supervisor, isn't it? I really hope you don't think I'm... well, that I'm losing my mind or anything, Doctor. I'm just a regular guy who wants to get his words straight.
Do you use alcohol or any other substances regularly?

Oh, no, Doctor, not at all. I mean... I know some folks might have a few drinks to unwind after a long shift at the store, but I really don't. Maybe, um, maybe a glass of wine at a wedding or a holiday dinner, but that's really it. 

And definitely no other substances, I promise. I always want to make sure I have a clear head for the team, you know? You have to set a good example when you're the supervisor, especially for the younger workers. I just try to take good care of my health and do the right thing. That's the best way to be, don't you think? I really try to be responsible about all that.
Are you having trouble with everyday tasks because of the way your words are jumping around when you talk?

Well, um... I guess it has made things a little tricky lately. But I really am trying my best to keep on top of everything, I promise. 

It's just... well, at work, they kind of stopped putting me on the busy weekend shifts. My boss mentioned something in my last performance review about... um, maybe needing to take a step back or even a suspension if my communication doesn't clear up. But I think they're just being extra cautious, you know? They just want the store to run smoothly, which I completely understand. 

And at home... my wife has been so wonderful. She's been taking care of a few things I usually handle, like some of our social commitments. I think some folks were just getting a little confused when I'd talk, and I never want to make anyone uncomfortable. It's just a temporary bump in the road, right? I'm sure once we figure out why my words are getting a little tangled, everything will go right back to normal. That makes sense, doesn't it, Doctor? I just want to get back to doing a good job for everyone.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened recently?

Oh, no, my memory is just fine, Doctor. Really, it is. I mean, sure, everyone misplaces their keys now and then, or forgets why they walked into a room, right? But I haven't noticed any real trouble remembering things that just happened. 

I always make sure to keep a little notepad in my pocket at the store, just to jot down inventory numbers or things my team tells me, but that's just being organized. It's not because I'm forgetting things. A good supervisor has to stay on top of the details, you know? So I just like to be thorough. My mind is still sharp, I promise. That's pretty typical for someone my age to use a notepad, wouldn't you say? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything the right way.
Do you feel anxious or stressed when you're trying to communicate and your words start jumping around?

Well, um... maybe just a little bit? But really, it's nothing I can't handle, Doctor. I promise. 

I mean, I suppose anyone might feel a tiny bit flustered if they're trying to explain a display change to the team and the words don't come out exactly the way they meant. But I try not to let it get to me. I just take a deep breath, smile, and try again. You have to keep a positive attitude, right? 

I don't want to make a big fuss over it or let the team see me looking stressed. A good supervisor has to stay calm under pressure. So, sure, maybe it's a little frustrating sometimes, but I wouldn't call it real anxiety or anything like that. I'm doing my best to manage it gracefully. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just staying positive and pushing through?
Have you noticed any changes in how your friends or family interact with you when you're having trouble with your words?

Well, um, I guess it goes back to what I was mentioning a little earlier, Doctor. Everyone has just been... well, really helpful, honestly. My wife, for instance, she's been an absolute angel. I think she noticed that some of our friends were getting a little, um, quiet or maybe a bit confused or uncomfortable when my sentences would get tangled up. So she's just been stepping in and covering a lot of the social commitments I used to handle. She just smooths it all over so no one feels awkward, which is just wonderful of her, don't you think? 

And I suppose my work family has changed their approach a little bit too. Like I said before, my boss just doesn't quite trust me to run those busy weekend shifts right now, and... well, he did give me that warning about a possible suspension after my review if things don't improve. But I really think they're just trying to protect the store's reputation while I get this little issue sorted out. They're just being supportive in their own way, making sure I don't get overwhelmed. It's completely normal for people to step in and help out like that, right? I just feel very blessed that they're all being so patient with me while I work on getting back to my old self.
Do you find that your words jump around like that when you're talking to friends or family about things that have nothing to do with work?

Oh, um... no, I haven't really noticed it happening then. When I'm just relaxing at home with my wife, or chatting with a neighbor about the yard, things are pretty easygoing. I think the words just flow a lot better when there's no pressure, you know? 

It seems like it's mostly just at the store where things get a little... tangled up. But at home, talking about regular, everyday things, I'm just my normal self. I mean, sure, everyone stumbles over a word now and then if they've had a long day, but I wouldn't say my words jump around with my family. That sounds pretty normal, doesn't it? Just being a little more relaxed and clear when you're off the clock?
Do you find that your words jump around more when discussing specific topics, like work-related issues, as opposed to other subjects?

Well, um, I suppose... yes, it does seem to happen a bit more when we're talking about the store. But I think that's just because work is... well, it's just a lot more complicated than figuring out what to have for dinner, right? 

When I'm trying to explain the new inventory system or the shift schedules, there are just so many moving parts. It makes sense that my brain might try to rush ahead and get a little mixed up. I really don't think it's anything to worry about, Doctor. It's just a sign that I care so much about getting my job right, you know? Anyone would get a little tongue-tied when they're trying to manage all those important details. That's a perfectly normal reaction to a busy job, wouldn't you agree? I'm sure it's just temporary.
Do you think there's something specific about being at work that makes your words jump around more than when you're not at work?

Well, um... I'm really not sure if there's one specific thing, honestly. I haven't noticed any particular trigger or anything like that. 

Like I was saying, it's just... well, retail is a very fast-paced environment. You've got customers asking questions, the phones ringing, making sure the floor is covered... it's just a lot of noise and activity all at once. So, I don't think it's anything unusual about the store itself, just the normal hustle and bustle of being a supervisor. 

I mean, anyone's brain would get a little tired trying to keep up with all of that, don't you think? It's just normal fatigue, I'm sure of it. Am I giving you the kind of information you need, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and answering your questions the right way.
Do you think your words jump around more when you're feeling stressed or anxious at work?

Stressed? Oh, um... I wouldn't really say I get anxious. I mean, I've been doing this a long time, so I know how to handle the floor. 

I don't think it's stress, exactly. Maybe just... well, just trying to get everything done at once, you know? I haven't really noticed it being tied to feeling nervous or anything like that. It's just a demanding job, and sometimes your mouth just tries to move as fast as the store does. 

I hope I'm not making it sound like I can't handle my responsibilities, because I really do a good job there. I keep everything running smoothly. Does that make sense, Doctor? I'm trying my best to explain it clearly for you, I just wouldn't want you to think I'm overwhelmed when I'm really just being a dedicated worker.
Is there a particular task at work where your words jump around the most?

Well, um... I guess if I had to pick a specific task, it might be when I'm trying to go over the inventory numbers with the team, or maybe when we're setting up the weekend schedule. 

I mean, it's just a lot of details, right? So sometimes I'll start talking about the delivery trucks, and then I'll realize I need to mention Thursday's shift, and then somehow that reminds me of the church grill we're setting up for the weekend... and then I might mention my boss's tone of voice about the whole thing. 

I guess... well, I guess sometimes people look at me like they can't quite follow what I'm saying. But I think that's just because I have so much information in my head that I'm trying to share all at once to be helpful. It's not that I'm confused, I just want to make sure everyone has all the details. I hope that's okay to say, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right examples so you can see how hard I work to keep everything organized.
Do you think the pressure to perform well as a supervisor contributes to your words jumping around?

Pressure? Oh, well... no, I wouldn't really use that word. I don't feel pressured, exactly. I mean, I've been managing people for quite a while now, and I know exactly what's expected of me. 

I really wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, buckling under the weight of the job or anything like that. I take a lot of pride in being a reliable supervisor. So... no, I haven't noticed that the expectations themselves make my words get tangled up. It's really just the sheer number of moving parts I have to keep track of to be helpful to the team, like I was saying before. 

I handle the actual responsibilities just fine, I promise. Am I explaining that okay, Doctor? I just want to make absolutely sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are, and that I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.
Do you ever find it hard to stop talking about a particular topic once you've started?

Hard to stop? Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I try to be very mindful of other people's time, especially at work. 

Sometimes I might go into a little more detail than someone else might, but that's really just because I want to make sure I'm being thorough, you know? I want to make sure I'm covering all the bases so nothing falls through the cracks. But I definitely don't just keep talking and talking if someone else needs to get a word in. I know how to read a room and keep things moving. 

I hope I'm not coming across as someone who just rambles on without paying attention to anyone else. I always try to be a good listener too. Does that make sense, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you find that your words jump around more when you're trying to explain a specific idea or concept?

Explain a specific idea? Um, well... I'm not really sure if it's tied to one particular concept or anything like that. 

I mean, I try very hard to be clear when I'm explaining things to the team. If I'm going over a new store policy or something, I want to make sure I'm doing a good job and getting it right. I don't think my words get more jumbled just because the idea is specific. I really do my best to lay it all out neatly for them. 

I haven't really noticed a pattern like that, to be honest. I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, Doctor. I really am trying my best to be helpful and clear for you.
Have you recently started or stopped taking any medications that might be affecting your speech?

Medications? Oh, um... no. No, I haven't started anything new or stopped anything. 

I'm very careful about that sort of thing. I definitely wouldn't just stop taking something on my own without checking first—I know how important it is to be responsible with your health, especially when you have a team relying on you at work. So, no, there haven't been any changes at all. I take all of that very seriously, I promise. 

Is that what you needed to know, Doctor? I just want to make absolutely sure I'm giving you the right answers to help you figure everything out.
Have you used any substances, including alcohol, in the past 30 days?

Substances? Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I might have a glass of wine with dinner once in a blue moon, just to unwind, but that's it. Nothing else. 

I know how bad that stuff can be for you, and I really try to take good care of myself. I have to be sharp for the store, you know? The staff really looks up to me to set a good example, so I would never do anything to jeopardize that. I stay completely away from anything illegal or... or anything like that. 

I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient and giving you the right information. I really appreciate you taking the time to ask all these questions.
Do you think your speech would be clearer if you had a drink or used a substance?

Oh, a drink to make it clearer? Um... no, I don't think so. I really don't. 

I mean, alcohol usually makes people a little sloppy, doesn't it? I would never want to rely on something like that to communicate better. I always try to handle things with a clear head, especially because I need to be professional for my team. I wouldn't want to give the wrong impression or... or seem like I can't handle my responsibilities on my own. 

I just try to do my best naturally, you know? I hope that makes sense, Doctor. I really wouldn't want you to think I'd turn to something like that to fix things. I'm trying to do everything the right way.
Have you ever noticed that your words jump around less when you've had a drink?

Oh, um... no. No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. Like I was saying before, I just don't drink enough to really test something like that out. Just that occasional glass of wine with dinner... so I wouldn't really know if it changes how my words come out. 

Plus, I try extremely hard to just focus and speak clearly on my own. I have to be a good communicator for the store, so I wouldn't want to rely on a drink to fix things. That wouldn't be very responsible, would it? 

So, no, I haven't noticed any difference. I hope that's helpful? I'm really trying to give you the best answers I can, Doctor. Am I doing okay with all of this?
